## Write side — keeping the index in step

When someone edits an issue title, the edit goes through the `updateIssueAction` Server Action in `src/actions/issues/update-issue.ts`, which (after a `can(actor, "issue:update", ...)` check) calls `updateIssue()` in `src/server/services/issue-service.ts`. That function re-checks `assertOrgScope` and `assertCan`, applies the write via `issueRepo.updateIssue(input)`, and then calls `emit("issue.updated", { issueId, projectId, changedFields, ... })` from `src/lib/event-bus.ts`.

`emit()` is a fire-and-await publish: it looks up every handler registered for `"issue.updated"` and runs them with `Promise.allSettled`, so one throwing handler can never abort the write or block a sibling handler. The subscribers are all wired once at process start by `registerEventHandlers()` in `src/server/services/event-registry.ts` (invoked from `src/instrumentation.ts`), which calls `registerSearchListeners()` in `src/server/services/search-service.ts` among others.

Inside `registerSearchListeners()`, the `"issue.updated"` handler does *not* trust the event payload for content — it re-reads the row with `issueRepo.findIssueById(payload.orgId, payload.issueId)` and, if found, calls `indexIssue(orgId, issue)`. That function builds the searchable text as `[issue.title, issue.description ?? ""].join("\n")` and calls `searchRepo.upsertSearchDocument()` in `src/server/repositories/search-repository.ts`. That function upserts the row keyed by `(orgId, subjectKind, subjectId)` rather than by the index row's own id — it `select`s for an existing match and either `update`s `content`/`projectId`/`indexedAt` or `insert`s a fresh row — which is what makes repeated re-indexing (from `issue.created`, `issue.updated`, or the `search.reindex_requested` drift-repair event) idempotent. So the "searchable copy" is the `searchIndex` table, holding one denormalized row per subject: `id`, `orgId`, `subjectKind`, `subjectId`, `projectId`, `content` (title+description concatenated), and `indexedAt`. This is the whole write-time path a colleague's search benefits from moments after the title edit commits.

## Read side — what a query goes through

Two entry points share identical gating "deliberately duplicated," per the comment in `src/app/api/search/route.ts`: the command-palette `GET` route (fires on every keystroke, plain `fetch`) and the `searchAction` Server Action in `src/actions/search/search.ts` (used by the search page). Both resolve an `Actor` (`getActor`/`withAction`), check `can(actor, "org:read", ...)`, load the org via `getOrganizationSummary`, build a `FlagContext` with `buildFlagContext`, and decide whether `"advanced_search"` is enabled (`isEnabled` in `src/lib/feature-flags.ts`) to narrow the requested `kinds` (comments excluded unless advanced search is on) before calling `search()` in `src/server/services/search-service.ts`.

`search()` re-derives the gating independently rather than trusting the caller:
1. `assertOrgScope(actor, input.orgId)` — rejects if the query's org doesn't match the actor's own org (`TenantScopeError` from `src/lib/tenant.ts`).
2. `assertCan(actor, "issue:read", orgResource(input.orgId))` — permission check.
3. `consumeRateLimit(input.orgId, "search:query")` from `src/lib/rate-limit.ts` — a token bucket (base capacity 120, refill 60/min, scaled by the org's plan via `configFor`). If the bucket is empty, `search()` throws `"Search rate limit reached; try again after ${resetAt}"` — a perfectly well-formed query gets refused here purely on request volume.
4. It re-evaluates `isEnabled("advanced_search", ...)` itself, then checks `input.q.includes(":")`: field-scoped syntax like `status:done` is an `advanced_search`-only feature, so on a plan/flag that doesn't include it, a colon in the query throws `"Field-scoped search is not included in this plan"` rather than being treated as literal text — the second circumstance where a valid-looking query is refused.
5. Only after all of that does it call `searchRepo.searchDocuments(input)`.

`searchDocuments()` builds filters with `orgPredicate` (tenant scoping), a `LIKE %q%` substring match on `content`, an optional `subjectKind` `inArray`, and an optional `projectId` filter, runs a keyset-paginated query (`keysetPredicate`/`toPage` from `_paging.ts`) ordered by `indexedAt`/`id`, and returns the matching `SearchIndexRow`s. Back in `search()`, each row is mapped to a `SearchHit`: `title` is the first line of `content` (so the title/description join done at index time is undone by splitting on `"\n"`), `snippet` is computed by `snippetAround()` (60 characters of context on each side of the match), and `href` is built by `hrefFor()`.

Two additional refusal paths sit above all this: the API route separately checks `isEnabled("command_palette", context)` and returns a `forbidden` JSON response if that flag is off, and both entry points return a `validation_failed` result if `searchQuerySchema` (in `src/schemas/search.ts`) rejects the raw input (e.g. empty or >200-char `q`) before `search()` is ever called.
